title: Real-world project cookbook
summary: Source-backed recipes from basic control to safer multi-peripheral devices.
body: Recipes progress from a small verified circuit to robust behavior. Confirm that every selected peripheral page reports the required runtime adapter as supported.

• [[cookbook.basic-patterns|Basic automation patterns]] — buttons, relays, timers, MQTT, display, battery, and audio.
  • [[cookbook.control-systems|Lighting, gate, alarm, and multi-sensor designs]].
  • [[cookbook.thermostat|Thermostat]] — hysteresis, timing, MQTT, and failure policy.
  • [[cookbook.water-system|Water system]] — level alarms, filling, timeout, and overflow.
  • [[cookbook.drv8833|DRV8833 motor]] — direction, limits, and MQTT.
  • [[cookbook.mini-piano|Mini piano]] — recorded melodies through DAC or buzzer.

Support rule

Some recipes explain a useful design while flagging unavailable drivers. A profile in Configuration is not automatically executable in firmware.

title: Complete thermostat: basic to robust
summary: Cooling control with hysteresis, timing protection, MQTT, and explicit failure behavior.
body:
Hardware and support

Use a temperature source that exposes a firmware Logics value and a relay profile that exposes ON/OFF. The relay adapter is implemented. The current DS18B20 profile is available for wiring, but its automatic firmware Logics adapter is not currently supported; do not claim a working DS18B20 thermostat until that adapter exists.
Test with a low-voltage indicator. A heater, compressor, or mains fan needs rated control hardware and independent safety protection.

Version 1 — crossing the upper threshold

Temperature → Compare A (> 30 °C) → Result → Rising Edge
Rising Edge Out → Relay ON In

This turns on once above 30 °C; it does not define OFF.

Version 2 — hysteresis

Temperature > 30 °C → Rising Edge → Relay ON
Temperature < 27 °C → Rising Edge → Relay OFF

Between 27 and 30 °C, the previous state remains. This prevents chatter around one threshold.

Version 3 — timing

Cooldown suppresses repeat triggers and Delay postpones an action. There is no single dedicated compressor minimum-ON/minimum-OFF state-machine block. Model and test both directions explicitly, or use a rated external controller where mandatory protection is required.

Version 4 — MQTT

On Start → Timer 10 s → MQTT Publish In
Temperature → Append value
Topic: elma/hvac/temperature

Relay State → On Change → MQTT Publish
Topic: elma/hvac/cooling_state

Version 5 — failure policy

If the driver exposes Available/Error, route failure to the explicitly chosen safe relay action and an MQTT alarm. ELMA-IoT cannot infer whether ON or OFF is safe. Hardware cut-outs remain independent.

Test matrix

  1. Verify ON above 30 and OFF below 27.
  2. Power-cycle in each state.
  3. Disconnect sensor and broker separately.
  4. Confirm a software halt cannot create an unsafe physical condition.

title: Water level, alarm, and filling controller
summary: Binary and continuous level systems with timeout, overflow, and failure behavior.
body:
Choose the measurement

A float/reed switch is binary: high/not-high. An analog sensor is continuous but needs calibration and a supported ADC runtime value. Ultrasonic ranging is not currently represented by a built-in profile/driver.

Support boundary

Reed-switch State/Rising/Falling is supported. The water-leak/rain profile is configuration-only in the current runtime policy. A generic analog level driver is not currently supported unless represented by a supported analog input adapter.

Simple alarm

Low-level switch State → edge matching wiring polarity
Edge → MQTT Publish: elma/tank/low_alarm

Automatic filling

Low switch active → Rising Edge → Pump relay ON
High switch active → Rising Edge → Pump relay OFF

Use a driver rated for the pump control circuit; test polarity with the pump disconnected.

Safer filling

  • Maximum runtime path commands OFF.
  • Separate overflow switch always commands OFF.
  • Cooldown rate-limits MQTT alarms.
  • Contradictory or missing switches have an explicit safe state.
  • Independent dry-run/current protection is required where damage is possible; there is no built-in current-based dry-run detector.

Test

Test low only, high only, both, neither, stuck/unplugged switch, restart while filling, network loss, and maximum runtime.

title: DRV8833 DC motor control
summary: Wire and operate the implemented two-channel DRV8833 runtime safely.
body:
What it is

DRV8833 is a dual H-bridge. GPIO selects direction while a separate supply provides motor current. Never connect a motor directly to ESP GPIO.

Wiring

DRV8833Role
IN1/IN2Channel A direction GPIO
IN3/IN4Channel B direction GPIO
VMExternal motor supply
GNDMotor and ESP reference ground
AOUT/BOUTMotor terminals, never GPIO

Implemented behavior

The Motor page runs either channel forward/backward for 100–600,000 ms; default 5,000 ms. It drives the inactive input LOW, then active HIGH. It stops on duration, manual request, or configured limit input. Directions may be labelled Opening/Closing; learned state supports Toggle. MQTT supports open, close, switch, and duration.

PWM speed

Not currently supported by the DRV8833 motor runtime. Current code uses digital direction pins and timed movement. Do not treat PWM speed, braking modes, or current regulation as available controls.

Progressive test

  1. Verify safe pin assignments with motor disconnected.
  2. Connect one suitable low-current motor.
  3. Run forward 500 ms; after stopping, reverse 500 ms.
  4. Add end switches and verify an active limit rejects movement.
  5. Increase duration only after limits and emergency power removal work.

Heat and resets

Heat suggests excess/stall current, a short, or inadequate cooling. ESP resets suggest supply droop/noise. Size for stall current and follow the module’s decoupling guidance.

title: Build a mini piano
summary: Record notes and play them through a supported DAC or buzzer.
body:
Implemented instrument

Piano melody has one octave C through the next C, octave 1–7, instrument choice, and one recording per block. Recording again replaces that block; add blocks for more melodies.

Controls

White PC keys: A S D F G H J K. Black: W E T Y U. Number keys select octave; comma/period or arrows step octaves. Mouse/touch animates. Limit: 128 events and 60 seconds per block.

Polyphony

Holding keys records chords. DAC/I2S can render polyphony. A passive buzzer is physically monophonic; an active buzzer makes its own fixed tone and cannot reproduce arbitrary notes.

Workflow

  1. Configure a supported output and all pins.
  2. Add Piano and the configured Play block.
  3. Connect Melody to Source.
  4. Connect a Flow event to Play In.
  5. Record, preview, save, compile, and test.
Button Rising Edge → Audio Play In
Piano Melody → Audio Play Source

Physical keys

Supported button edges can trigger separate stored melodies. A direct arbitrary frequency API is not currently supported; use one short melody block per note/chord.
